newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-GILLESPIE LEADS AUSTRALIAN FIGHTBACK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GILLESPIE LEADS AUSTRALIAN FIGHTBACK.

text.p: Three quick wickets from fast bowler Jason Gillespie helped reduce South Africa to 137 for six and gave Australia a much-needed lift in the second test against South Africa on Sunday.
Gillespie, who took five for 54 in the first innings, went to lunch on the third day with figures of three for 36, as South Africa held an overall lead of 238.
Resuming on 83 without loss, South Africa quickly lost Gary Kirsten, who had added just two to his overnight 41, when he missed a straight delivery from Gillespie that kept low.

Jacques Kallis then perished for two to an inspirational piece of fielding from Greg Blewett at square leg. A swooping pick-up and direct hit left Kallis stranded by a metre after attempting a quick single.

Opener Adam Bacher was the next to go, top-edging a hook off Gillespie straight to Glenn McGrath on the fine leg boundary. Bacher's 49 lasted nearly three hours and contained seven boundaries from 129 deliveries.
In Gillespie's next over, his seventh of the morning, he trapped Daryll Cullinan lbw for two with a rapid off-cutter that beat the batsman for both pace and movement.

When Herschelle Gibbs was caught at second slip by Mark Waugh off Glenn McGrath for seven, South Africa had collapsed from 87 without loss to 122 for five and Australia were firmly back in the contest.

Hansie Cronje and Brian McMillan steadied the ship with half an hour of solid resistance but McMillan, first innings rescuer with 55, missed a pull shot against a Michael Bevan long hop and fell lbw for two in the final over before the interval.
South Africa's main hope of a match-winning lead on an improving pitch lay in Cronje who twice pulled McGrath through midwicket for four. He was 25 not out at lunch.
